$schema_note: Demo manifest consumed by the OmniSim Launcher Robot Window. To add a new demo: add an entry here AND a row in /DEMOS.md. Paths are relative to the repo root.

categories.label: Starter
categories.description: Hello-world demos — start here if you've never opened OmniSim before.

demos.name: Warehouse Husky
demos.blurb: The onboarding demo. Husky random-walks a 30 × 18 m warehouse with collision recovery.

demos.name: SO101 physical pick and place
demos.blurb: An authored simulation trajectory pinches a cube, carries it and releases it into a box. Includes an open-gripper control. This is not a replay of the real LeRobot recording.

demos.name: OmniArm 6 real pick and place
demos.blurb: The self-contained CLI and BETA starter: a friction grasp lifts and places a block, with a drop control (PICK_CONTROL_DROP=1) that must fail.

categories.label: Debugging — find out why a robot failed
categories.description: A cell with a real, reproducible fault in it. Load the faulty world, watch GET /sim/events, and find the bug without a screenshot or the world source.

demos.name: The arm drops the box two times in five
demos.blurb: DELIBERATELY BROKEN. One physics field is wrong and the gripper loses the part in mid-air on the two heaviest of five payloads — while a screenshot of the end state still looks fine. Diagnose it from the event stream alone: RUN: python scripts/dev/diagnose_drop.py projects/samples/demos/worlds/debug/omniarm6_drop_fault.omniworld

demos.name: The same cell, with the fault fixed
demos.blurb: The verified fix: the same world with newtonGroundMu back at 6. All five payloads are carried and placed. Sweep both to see 3/5 become 5/5: RUN: python scripts/dev/drop_payload_sweep.py --both

demos.name: ALOHA recorded battery replay (diagnostic)
demos.blurb: Recorded ALOHA motions in an estimated scene. The recorded actions do not reproduce the insertion. A separate authored physical task and real-video comparison are documented in projects/robots/trossen/aloha/README.md.

categories.label: Chat · Arms
categories.description: OmniLink chat requires an OmniKey and a connected model. Natural-language console for a robot arm: right-click the robot -> Show Robot Window -> type 'home', 'wave hello', 'joint 3 to 1.5'.

demos.name: OmniArm 6
demos.blurb: 6-axis OmniArm 6 cobot with a natural-language console. Type 'home' or 'wave hello'; the arm holds pose under gravity.

demos.name: OmniArm 6 + 140 mm two-finger gripper (real grasp)
demos.blurb: Ask it to "pick up the block" and "put it down" -- and the hold is REAL friction, not the kinematic weld every other chat demo uses. Say "open the gripper" mid-carry and the block falls, which is the point.

demos.name: Talk to Ari (OmniArm 6 + Robotiq 2F-85)
demos.blurb: The same OmniArm 6 with a persona: right-click -> Talk to the Robot for the in-sim chat card. Ask Ari to pick up a coloured cube and the real 2F-85 fingers close on it, lift and carry -- the cubes are rigid bodies and fall when released. The one chat world whose name is not omnilink_<robot>. RUN: powershell -File projects/samples/demos/worlds/chat/run_omniarm6_talk.ps1

categories.label: Chat · Quadrupeds
categories.description: OmniLink chat requires an OmniKey and a connected model. Six quadrupeds on one bridge (omnilink_quadruped_bridge): poses — "stand", "sit", "wave hello" — on all of them, plus real wheeled driving on the M20 family. There is no learned gait behind any of these: "walk" cycles the legs in place.

demos.name: OmniQuad
demos.blurb: OmniQuad — poses only. Try "stand", "sit", "wave hello".

demos.name: Deep Robotics Lite3
demos.blurb: 11.9 kg quadruped that settles out of its spawn pose onto its own physics and holds a 0.262 m stance — no supervisor pin. Try "stand", "sit", "wave hello"; "walk" cycles the legs in place. Package provenance: projects/robots/deep_robotics/PROVENANCE.md (BSD-3, no affiliation).

demos.name: Deep Robotics X30
demos.blurb: The Lite3's 55.8 kg sibling, standing at 0.395 m on the same bridge and the same sentences. Five times the mass is the difference you can watch settle.

demos.name: Deep Robotics M20 (wheeled-legged)
demos.blurb: Wheeled-legged: "drive forward" turns four real continuous wheel joints and the 34.5 kg body actually rolls (0.48 m/s measured), rather than cycling legs on the spot. Poses work as on the Lite3.

demos.name: Deep Robotics M20S
demos.blurb: The higher-torque M20 — identical geometry and meshes upstream, different effort and velocity limits. Same wheeled-legged surface; useful next to the M20 as an actuator-limit A/B.

demos.name: Deep Robotics M20 + AgileX Piper arm
demos.blurb: The M20 carrying a 6-DoF AgileX Piper arm and gripper (39.2 kg all in). The BASE drives and poses as on the M20; the arm is loaded and holds its zero pose — the quadruped bridge does not command it, so do not ask this one to pick anything up.

categories.label: G1 skills & BATON sequences
categories.description: The flagship G1 robotics demos (walk, carry, turn, climb). RUN THESE FROM A SHELL, NOT THE LAUNCH BUTTON: each needs a large deploy env (engine hook + ghost LUTs + corridors + harness + BATON course) that a bare world load cannot carry — clicking Launch opens the scene but shows a LIFELESS robot. Every blurb below gives the bash one-liner. Catalogue CLI: python projects/policies/skills/skill_lib.py list (15 skills + 6 BATON sequences). HARNESS DISCLOSURE: rows marked CRANED run on a weight-bearing puppet harness (up to 700 N up ~= 2x the 34 kg G1's weight, +/-350 N.m attitude) — a real-footwork but NOT free-standing walk. The stair climb is the exception: HARNESS_KZ=0, the legs do the lifting. Details + honest status: DEMOS.md section 2.

demos.name: G1 box delivery (BATON headliner)
demos.blurb: RUN: bash projects/policies/demos/run_box_delivery.sh  — G1 walks to cart A, picks a real 1.5 kg box, carries it to cart B, sets it down on real contact, takes a real ~90-deg footwork corner, walks away. 0 falls. CRANED. Corner certified only in the 0->90 deg band.

demos.name: G1 box delivery — classic
demos.blurb: RUN: bash projects/policies/demos/run_box_delivery_classic.sh  — the verified baseline delivery: walk, stand, pick the real 1.5 kg box, carry, place, walk on, stand. 0 falls, no corner. CRANED.

demos.name: G1 walk -> turn -> walk
demos.blurb: RUN: bash projects/policies/demos/run_walk_turn_walk.sh  — walks ~5 m, turns a real ~90 deg by FOOTWORK (no crane yaw; lands 90.6-95.6 deg actual), then a clean straight leg on the new heading. 3/3, 0 falls. CRANED.

demos.name: G1 footwork turn (solo)
demos.blurb: RUN: bash projects/policies/demos/run_turn_solo.sh  — the footwork-turn policy by itself: settle to a stand, turn ~90 deg on pure footwork (wtz=0), decel, hold. EXPERIMENTAL per the skill registry. CRANED.

demos.name: G1 stair climb + summit stand
demos.blurb: RUN: bash projects/policies/demos/run_climb_stairs_stand.sh  — climbs the full 5 treads (3 cm risers) LEGS-ONLY (HARNESS_KZ=0, no vertical assist), then a position-gated BATON handover holds a verified motionless stand on the top landing. CAP: 3 cm is the measured ceiling (4 cm ~= 2 steps, 5 cm ~= 0).

demos.name: G1 stair climb (5 treads @ 3 cm)
demos.blurb: RUN: bash projects/policies/demos/run_climb_stairs.sh  — real foot steps up 5 treads, LEGS-ONLY (HARNESS_KZ=0), base z 0.72->0.88. Stairs are NOT solved: 3 cm is the measured ceiling for the stock-foot G1 (4 cm ~= 2 steps, 5 cm ~= 0).

demos.name: G1 'decent walker' (flagship walk)
demos.blurb: RUN: powershell -File projects/policies/worlds/run_g1_decent_walker.ps1  — G1 walks the official Unitree gait beside its ghost hologram (WBMATCH4 0.868). CRANED (visible puppet harness). Long straights still have a residual live fall rate.

demos.name: G1 box grasp (physics arms)
demos.blurb: RUN: bash projects/policies/demos/run_box_grasp.sh  — EXPERIMENTAL / BLOCKED (the script says so): G1 picks up a real Newton box with its ARMS, zero kinematic writes. Blocked on a warp contact-kernel defect near the cart. The shipping pick-and-place demo is box delivery.

categories.label: Showcase
categories.description: Self-running visual showcases — sit back and watch, or follow a robot with F5.

demos.name: ORC: Foundry
demos.blurb: Pilot ANVIL against RAZOR in an industrial yard. ENTER starts, WASD drives, SPACE toggles the weapon, C changes camera, TAB switches autopilot. Contact-driven damage and moving debris. For GPU temperature protection use ORC's Launch Foundry.bat instead of this launcher.

demos.name: Metazoa (robot cells that grow into robots)
demos.blurb: Identical 12 cm hinge-cell robots dock face to face into walking organisms: a head rudder steers, a pitch wave inchworms, bodies back into free cells to recruit them, divide at eight cells, and every cell is conserved. Physics-real welds, one supervisor.

demos.name: Living ecosystem (alife)
demos.blurb: Evolved quadruped creatures that sense food, steer to it, eat, breed and starve in one live world. One supervisor drives every body; species bodies evolve between epochs.

demos.name: OmniLink Warehouse (OmniArm 6 + OmniTug 500 crew)
demos.blurb: The flagship production line: a vacuum-gripper OmniArm 6 picks onto trolleys while two OmniTug 500 tugs dispatch and return them.

demos.name: OmniArm 6 bin picking + colour sort
demos.blurb: Camera-driven bin picking: the arm empties a randomly-filled bin and sorts the parts by colour.

demos.name: The Living City
demos.blurb: Generator-driven 4x4 city: 48 cars with traffic signals, pedestrians, a bus, day/night cycle. Click a car, then right-click -> Follow Object.
